content.text: Do a deep dive on the docs and code and rewrite all docs to describe the features of the app
<skill-format>true</skill-format>

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

# Frame Job

A native macOS video editor: open a movie, arrange it on
layered tracks over a fixed canvas, trim, split, annotate, animate, export.
Swift/AppKit UI over a Rust core — the core decides, AVFoundation and Metal do.
Apple Silicon, macOS 26+.

The opening flow is the point. File ▸ Open on a `.mov` or `.mp4` (or a drop on
the Dock icon, or the welcome window's Open Video…) creates an *untitled*
project sized and rated to that file, with the file as the first clip on
Track 1, ready to cut. Save then writes a `.framejob` package next to the
source.

The full design and implementation spec is `designs/spec/`, one file per
section, indexed by its `README.md`. It is normative: §5.2 is the project
schema, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture.

## What it does today

- **One kind of track.** Every track holds any clip — video, audio, image,
  text, shape. Tracks stack back to front; `tracks[0]` is the back.
- **Screen recording.** File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N, or the welcome window's
  third button) opens a small floating panel: a display or a window (the
  system picker), whether Frame Job's own windows are in a display recording
  (left out by default), a microphone with a live meter, system audio, click
  rings, 30 or 60 fps, point or pixel size, and where it lands — a new project, or
  an open document at its playhead. A 3-2-1 countdown, then a red dot with
  the elapsed time in the menu bar carries Pause, Resume and Stop; File ▸
  Pause Recording pauses and resumes too. A paused recording is one file
  per stretch; a stretch whose file cannot be read is left out, and the
  note names it and where its files are — and its microphone, when it
  reads, still lands in the stretch's place. The file is written to
  `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` and imported as ordinary media (undo
  removes the clip, never the file); a microphone is a second file on its
  own Microphone track, aligned to the picture. A new project takes the
  rate you chose; a screen recording's own rate is whatever the screen did.
  The first time you press Record the app asks for the Screen Recording
  and Microphone grants; a later press without them opens System Settings
  at the grant's pane. An agent never asks and never opens it. Source ▸
  Microphone Only records a voice-over — the microphone alone, the panel
  staying up with its meter and a Pause button — onto a new back
  Microphone track at the playhead.
- **Timeline** with a frame-accurate ruler, filmstrips and waveforms from a
  per-media cache, three row heights, magnify/⌥-wheel zoom about the cursor,
  and gesture sessions for drag, trim, rate-stretch (⌥ on the end edge),
  slip (⌥⇧ on a body), roll (⌥⇧ on an edge), marquee select, playhead scrub
  (and Space plays and pauses from anywhere but a field being typed into),
  marker drag, audio fade handles and track reorder — each one undo step,
  each snapping to clip edges, markers and the playhead (N toggles, ⌘
  suppresses). Double-clicking an empty span closes that gap; a media row
  dropped with ⌥ inserts and with ⇧⌥ overwrites. Double-clicking a clip
  renames it in place, a labelled clip wears a 6 pt dot in its label's
  colour on its name strip (the tint still says the kind), and a track
  header has eye, speaker, lock and headphones — solo. Right-clicking a
  header or an empty lane opens that track's menu: the four toggles and
  Remove Track.
- **Canvas** with an `AVPlayerLayer` under a transparent overlay: move, scale,
  rotate and crop handles, line/arrow endpoint handles, safe-area guides,
  snapping to the canvas centre and edges, inline text editing (the field
  grows and wraps as you type, as the text will once applied; Return

questions.question: "All docs" covers very different kinds of file here. Which should the rewrite cover? (The README today is an 846-line run-on feature list mixed with build, layout and MCP notes; the spec, ADRs and CLAUDE.md files are agent rulebooks and decision history.)

options.label: User docs (Recommended)
options.description: Rewrite README.md as a clear product overview and add a feature guide under docs/ (one file per area: timeline, canvas, audio, grading, HDR, captions, graphics, recording, export, assistant, MCP…), every claim checked against the code. Spec, ADRs, CLAUDE.md, manual-checks left alone, except developer content moved out of the README into a developer doc.

options.label: User docs + spec
options.description: As above, and also bring the spec's feature-describing sections (§4, §5.2, §6, §9) in line with the code wherever they drifted. ADRs, archive and CLAUDE.md files untouched.

options.label: Everything
options.description: Also rewrite the ADRs, CLAUDE.md files and docs/manual-checks.md. This goes against the repo's rules: ADRs are decision history and CLAUDE.md files are the rulebook, so it would cost the rationale they record.

## Building

Requires Xcode 26 or later (the macOS 26 SDK), Rust (cargo), [xcodegen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen), and [bun](https://bun.sh) (the assistant helper, `agent/`, is built by every `make app`, typechecked by `make typecheck` and its price function tested by `make test`; without bun they fail rather than skip).

```sh
make app        # cargo build --release + xcodegen + xcodebuild → build/Build/Products/Release/Frame Job.app
make app-debug  # the Debug app the proofs can drive: "Frame Job Debug" (its own bundle id, com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug, and settings) → build/Build/Products/Debug/Frame Job Debug.app, seconds after a one-file edit
make dist       # make app, then the Distribution build (no dev tools; the assistant helper signed with the hardened runtime) → build/Build/Products/Distribution/Frame Job.app, checked (dist_check.py, then published_check.py, the check a published build gets)
make run        # build and launch
make test       # Rust core, graphics and MCP proxy tests, then the agent lane's proof (tools/proof/assistant_lane_proof.py), the prompt texts' checks (tools/proof/assistant_prompt_proof.py --probe), the price function in both readers (tools/proof/prices_proof.py, no network) and the proofs' ledger and monthly budgets (tools/proof/budget_proof.py, no network)
make lint       # cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings
make typecheck  # swiftc -typecheck of app/Sources — the ONLY authoritative Swift check, then agent/'s tsc --noEmit (through bun)
make gate       # the whole check, in order: typecheck (its four known warnings and no other), cargo fmt --check, lint, test, then app with the Release app's signature checked; stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and tools are unchanged since it last passed (build/gate/)
make project    # xcodegen generate, with the base version from VERSION
make prices     # regenerate agent/prices/anthropic.json from LiteLLM's price table (network); the file's only writer
```

`FrameJob.xcodeproj` is generated — run `make project` after editing
`project.yml`, and don't commit the project file. Use `make project` rather
than a bare `xcodegen generate`: it feeds the base version from `VERSION` into
the project, which a bare run leaves blank.

### Publishing a release

Pushing to the `publish` branch runs `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: it
archives the Distribution configuration signed with Developer ID, exports it,
checks the exported app (`tools/proof/published_check.py`), packs it into
`FrameJob.dmg`, notarizes and staples the DMG, and attaches it to a GitHub
Release tagged `v<version>`. The version is `VERSION` (MAJOR.MINOR) plus the
workflow's run number, and the build number is the run number, so bump
`VERSION` for a new minor line. A local build reads "0.2 (0)". The newest build is always at
`https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/FrameJob.dmg`
(while the repository is private, only for people with access to it).

The workflow runs no tests: run `make test` and `make dist` on what you push.

The signing and notarization credentials are secrets in the repository's
`publish` environment (Settings ▸ Environments), whose deployment branches are
restricted to `publish`: `DEVELOPER_ID_P12_BASE64` and
`DEVELOPER_ID_P12_PASSWORD` (the Developer ID Application certificate exported
with its private key as a `.p12`, base64-encoded, and the export password),
`KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD` (any random string), `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, and `ASC_KEY_ID`,
`ASC_ISSUER_ID` and `ASC_KEY_P8_BASE64` (an App Store Connect API key and its
`.p8`, base64-encoded). Local builds stay ad-hoc signed and need none of them.

## AI agent access (MCP)

Frame Job serves an MCP server (streamable HTTP) on a Unix socket it binds at
every launch, `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`. An MCP
client reaches it through `framejob-mcp`, the stdio helper inside the bundle,
which lists the tools without opening Frame Job and launches it in the
background on the first tool call that finds it not running.

**Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP — Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers
the helper with Claude Code on the clipboard, with the path of the bundle you
ran it from; the section also shows the helper's path:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
```

Claude Desktop takes the same helper in its `claude_desktop_config.json`:

# Frame Job

A native macOS video editor. Open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a
fixed canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. Every edit
you make in the window can also be made by an AI agent over MCP, or by the
built-in Assistant, and each one is an ordinary undo step.

Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or later. Open source, with no account to make: every
AI feature runs on your own API key (Anthropic for the Assistant, AssemblyAI
for cloud transcription), and everything else works without one.

## Open a movie and start cutting

**File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a `.mov` or `.mp4` — or a drop on the Dock icon, or
**Open Video…** in the Welcome window — creates an *untitled* project sized and
rated to that file, with the file as the first clip on Track 1, ready to cut. A
portrait phone clip opens portrait, and a 29.97 fps file stays 29.97. **Save**
then writes a `.framejob` package, offered next to the source.

## Features

**Projects and media.** Movies, sound and pictures from everything macOS plays,
plus WebM and MKV copied in without re-encoding; missing files relinked;
Consolidate Media copies footage into the package.
→ [Projects and media](docs/guide/projects-and-media.md)

**Timeline.** One kind of track that holds any clip; a frame-accurate ruler,
filmstrips and waveforms, zoom about the cursor, snapping, markers, an in/out
range, track mute, solo and lock, clip names and colour labels.
→ [The timeline and playback](docs/guide/timeline.md)

Frame Job serves its editor as MCP tools on a local socket only programs you
run can open. An MCP client reaches it through `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside
the app, which starts Frame Job in the background on the first tool call if it
is not running. **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP ▸ Copy MCP Command** puts the
Claude Code registration line on the clipboard, with your copy's path:

claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'

# Frame Job User Guide

Frame Job is a native macOS video editor for Apple Silicon Macs running
macOS 26 or later. You open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a fixed
canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. Every edit you
make in the window can also be made by an AI agent over MCP, or by the built-in
Assistant.

The quickest way in: **File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a movie makes an untitled project
sized and timed to it, with the movie on Track 1, ready to cut. Save writes a
`.framejob` package.

## The pages

Read the first four in order to learn the editor; the rest stand alone.

1. [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md) — starting, saving and opening projects, the `.framejob` package, the Document tab's canvas settings, importing files, the Media tab and relinking.
2. [The timeline and playback](timeline.md) — the editor window, tracks and their switches, the ruler and playhead, zoom, selection, snapping, markers, the in/out range and playback.
3. [Editing clips](editing.md) — placing, moving, trimming, slipping, splitting, deleting and closing gaps, copy and paste, and nests.
4. [Canvas, layers, text and shapes](canvas-and-layers.md) — placing a picture on the canvas, opacity, blend modes, shadows and filters, text, shape, image and background clips, and matte tracks.
5. [Motion, actions and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md) — actions that animate a clip's properties over time, motion presets, and transitions between clips.
6. [Speed, reverse and freeze frames](speed.md) — constant speed, fitting a clip to a length, rate stretch, speed ramps and their presets, reversing and freeze frames.
7. [Audio](audio.md) — clip levels, fades, ducking, noise reduction, compression, pan, mute and solo, Normalize and Synchronize Audio.
8. [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md) — cutting dead air and filler words out of a spoken recording in one step.
9. [Captions and transcription](captions.md) — importing and exporting captions, and transcribing speech on this Mac or with AssemblyAI into subtitles or word-by-word captions.
10. [Colour grading](color-grading.md) — the Color tab, wheels, curves, looks and LUTs, adjustment clips and qualifiers, Show Ungraded and the scopes.
11. [HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md) — how sources are read, camera log, SDR and HDR (HLG) projects, blending, and HDR and SDR deliverables.
12. [Motion graphics](graphics.md) — graphic clips, the built-in graphics, their properties in the inspector, and bringing in your own.
13. [Screen recording](screen-recording.md) — recording a display or a window with system audio, microphone and click rings, and recording voice-overs.
14. [Exporting](export.md) — the export sheet, its formats and settings, presets, the Export Queue, and saving single frames.
15. [The Assistant](assistant.md) — chatting with Claude in the inspector to edit the open project, on your own Anthropic key.
16. [Driving Frame Job from an AI agent (MCP)](mcp.md) — connecting an MCP client such as Claude Code, how calls behave, and every tool.
17. [Settings](settings.md) — the Settings window, the View choices Frame Job remembers, and where it keeps its files.
18. [Menus and keyboard shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md) — every menu command with its shortcut, and the keys, gestures and context menus that have no menu item.

Writing your own graphic module is covered by the
[graphics API reference](../graphics-api.md).

content.text:
I'd run it as one workflow with three passes: a mechanical scan, reading by concern, then adversarial verification. The result would be a ranked report, and nothing gets refactored until you've looked at it.

## What's in scope

| Area | Lines | Files |
|---|---|---|
| `app/Sources` (Swift) | 123k | 482 |
| `core/src` (Rust) | 32k | 110 |
| `graphic/src` + `mcp-proxy/src` | 2.9k | 18 |
| `tools/proof` (Python and Swift probes) | 244k | 375 |
| `core/tests` | — | 133 |

I'd cover the product code (Swift, Rust, the two small crates) in depth. `tools/proof` is the largest area, but it's measurement code with different trade-offs, so it would be a separate, lighter tier. `core/tests` would only be checked for repeated fixture setup.

## Pass 1: mechanical clone scan (me, inline, a few minutes)

A token-based clone detector over each language finds copy-paste blocks, including ones with identifiers renamed. That's either `npx jscpd` (downloaded as a throwaway tool) or a short Python script of my own in the scratchpad. The output is a list of file:line pairs ranked by size and number of copies. It's exhaustive but shallow: it misses logic that does the same thing in a different shape.

## Pass 2: semantic readers (about 8 agents, one per concern)

Each reader gets its area's hits from pass 1 and looks for logic that repeats in different shapes. Likely areas:

1. `AgentServer+*.swift` handlers: argument reading, refusal wording, how results are built.
2. `AgentCatalog*.swift`: catalog entries and descriptions built by hand.
3. Inspector sections (`ClipPane` sections and the panes): building controls, binding, sending edits.
4. Sheet controllers: Silence, Reverse progress, Synchronize, Export and others.
5. `EditorViewController+*` extensions: their validator arms, selection-to-op code, undo naming.
6. Core ops: target lookup, range checks, refusal sentences, nest/`scope` resolution, time arithmetic.
7. Rendering and export paths: CompositionBuilder, Exporter, reverse, ramp audio, the caches.
8. Graphics and mcp-proxy: `graphic/`, the proxy, and Swift's graphic glue.

## Pass 3: verification

Each candidate gets two skeptics, each trying to show it isn't worth doing:
- **Behaviour:** are the copies really identical, or do edge cases differ?
- **Design:** would one abstraction tie together code that changes for different reasons?

Survivors are scored on lines saved, number of sites, risk, and whether any frozen file or file at the size cap is involved. A final agent then checks coverage: which areas weren't read and which pass-1 hits went unexplained.

**The best finds are copies that have already drifted apart,** where one copy got a fix the other didn't. Those are probably bugs, and they'd be reported separately at the top.

## Deliberate duplication I wouldn't flag

The repo keeps some copies on purpose:
- **Mirrors that must stay in step:** each op is written down four times (`op_table.rs`, `ReelOps.swift`, the catalog, spec §6), and each FFI export three times (Rust export, header, `ReelCore.swift`). I'd only flag these where one copy could be generated from another, which `opTool` already does for op arguments.
- **`schema_vN.rs` snapshots:** frozen copies of old formats.
- **`agent/src`:** kept byte-identical with Rasterize, so it's out of bounds.
- **Historical proof instruments:** they build old copies of the source on purpose.
- **Spec §11 decisions:** these are never re-argued.

## What you'd get, and what happens next

- **A ranked report.** I'd publish it as a private page, since it's long and you'd want to scan it.
- **Then your pick:** the ones you choose become GitHub issues (`ai-drafted`, `low-priority`) or a refactor road map.
- **Each refactor goes through litecode on its own.** The extraction lands as a pure move, gated alone, under the size and frozen-file rules.

## Cost and what I need from you

It's roughly 8 readers, about 2 verifiers per candidate and one coverage check. Expect a few dozen agents, which is more than the usual medium size, because you asked for a deep pass.

Two decisions before I start:
1. Should `tools/proof` get the full treatment, the light tier, or be left out?
2. Is a report the stopping point, or should I file the confirmed findings as issues straight away?

1. Left out for now

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..." --label ai-drafted`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies. Every issue an agent creates carries `ai-drafted`, beside any triage label, and `low-priority` unless it is urgent (data loss or a corrupt project, a crash or hang, a secret leak — each reachable in ordinary use — or something blocking other work now).
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue. A spec (the output of `/to-spec`) gets the `spec` label and never `ready-for-agent`, whatever the skill says: that label is a work order to a polling agent, and a spec is an input. Only the tickets `/to-tickets` produces carry `ready-for-agent`.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.

name: litecode-stacked-phases
description: How to run many /litecode pipelines back to back in Reelcut when the user commits only on request - tree-object baselines, reader reviews mapped onto litecode's cast, residue pipelines, rule H
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-09-19/20 the user asked for four road-map items "using /litecode for
each phase" and ten pipelines ran back to back with NO commits between
them, because the user commits only when they ask. What made that work:

- **A baseline per pipeline.** Before each run, write the working tree to a
  git TREE object with a temporary index (`cp .git/index tmp;
  GIT_INDEX_FILE=tmp git add -A; GIT_INDEX_FILE=tmp git write-tree`) and put
  the hash in `request.md`. The run's diff is `git diff <tree>`. Untracked
  files show there as wholly deleted, which is noise: say so in the request,
  and give `git show <tree>:<path> | diff - <path>` for them.
- **A reader review fits litecode's fixed cast**: the designer writes the
  review PLAN (diffs, the questions verbatim, what is already known with
  citations, named mutants of TODAY's tree, never an old binary, which aborts
  the instruments), the implementer is the readers one question at a time and
  fixes survivors, the reviewer is the SCEPTIC told to refute findings and
  break fixes. Record the deviation (sequential readers, one sceptic).
- **litecode never runs a second fix pass.** When the second review still
  says fix-required, run a small RESIDUE pipeline for code or proof changes,
  and close prose nits by hand. Either way nothing stays only in the handoff
  directory: see [[write-findings-into-repo-documents]].
- **Rule H**: any command that could loop without bound (a reverted-fix test,
  a mutant, a stress call) runs under a hard wall-clock limit, kills only the
  process group it started, and records an expiry as the row's answer.
- **The sceptics' verdicts were mostly about the RECORD**: a sentence that
  claimed more than a run printed, a count that did not match its own list, a
  true threshold with a false explanation. Tell every stage: a number is
  written only when a run printed it, and a control is called a CONTROL.
- **A reader's fix is where the worst defect hid**: swapping a snapping
  argument reader for a plain one removed the only ceiling and `Int64.max`
  crashed the app. A fix that changes how an argument is read keeps its
  bounds and is tried at the extremes.

- **A big feature splits into pipelines by what can be PROVED alone**
  (C1, 2026-09-20/21: tolls, pure parts with a probe, the run with its MCP
  proof, the chrome, then live rows and the closing record, then the reader
  review). Draft the next pipeline's `request.md` while the current one
  runs, and finalise it with a "what the last pipeline found that binds you"
  section and the new baseline tree.
- **Subagents will not edit a `CLAUDE.md`, and should not.** A map entry or
  a rule clause a phase makes false is the orchestrator's to apply by hand,
  after the pipeline's last review, recorded in the tree and told to the
  user.
- **When a command is denied, stop that action** — report what is left
  (paths, the one command) and carry on with the rest; never route the same
  deletion through another tool.

**Why:** the user wants every item finished and everything findable, and is
not at the machine to answer between pipelines.
**How to apply:** reuse this shape for any multi-phase request; pass each
pipeline's lessons forward in the next `request.md`. See also
[[roadmap-phases-via-subagents]] and [[user-prefers-my-recommendation]].

<details><summary>Verification — behaviour lens: reject, worth lens: reject (real drift bug)</summary>

#### behaviour lens: reject

I read every site. The copies that really are the same are one-expression closures: `ReelTime.snapToFrame(ReelTime.ticks(seconds: max(s, 0)), fps: binding.canvas.fps)`. They are at AudioPane.swift 152-154 (fades), AudioPane.swift 195-197 (duck), TextPane.swift 370-372 (reveal) and VideoPane+Motion.swift 46-48 (no max). The same expression is also written inline at VideoPane+Transition.swift 105-108 and ActionLaneView.swift 194-195. This is idiomatic boilerplate with a single-line body, and a shared helper would remove about 8 lines net.

The clamp drift does not exist in practice. Every value reaches these closures through `inspectorValueRow`, whose `OptionFieldControl` clamps to [min, max] (OptionControls.swift 232). The `.derived` reset calls `ops(read())` on a stored value that is never negative. The Motion rows have min 0.1 (VideoPane+Motion.swift 96, 116, 166) and Transition has min 0.02 (VideoPane+Transition.swift 104). So `max(_, 0)` could never change a result, and leaving it out is not a bug.

Two of the listed sites do different work:
- AudioPane.swift 313-318 (compressor) takes MILLISECONDS and deliberately does not snap. Its doc comment at 300-305 explains this.
- TimelineSessions.swift 408-418 (the fade-handle drag) takes a pointer Ticks value, measures from an edge, caps it at the clip's span and then snaps. It does not convert seconds.

Neither could share a seconds→frame-ticks helper. Folding the compressor in as `rampTicks` would merge two different units.

The claim of drift against the core is a design inconsistency, not a copy that drifted. core/CLAUDE.md 917-926 and props_check.rs 325-331 say the core leaves fades, duck and compressor attack/release off the grid. The inspector snaps fades and duck on purpose: AudioPane.swift 300-302 says the compressor times are unsnapped "unlike every other time in this pane". The fade handle snaps to match, because fades are also the clip's corner handles (AudioPane.swift 148-149). The effect the candidate describes is real: a 0.01 s Duck Attack typed in the inspector stores 0, and 0.1 s at 24 fps stores 50000 ticks (0.083 s), while `set_audio` over MCP stores exactly what it is sent. It would serve the fades, duck, reveal, motion, transition and action-lane duration sites, for a net saving of about 8 lines. - TextPane.swift 370-372
- VideoPane+Motion.swift 46-48

The max(_, 0) in the Audio and Text copies is also redundant, since those rows use min 0.

content.text:
Issue #355 is about a difference in behaviour, not duplicated code. The inspector and the agent store different values for the same audio setting, and someone has to decide which one is right.

**The rule.** core/CLAUDE.md's Times rule says audio fades, the duck's attack and release, and the compressor's attack and release are deliberately kept off the frame grid. The reason it gives is that snapping them to a video frame "would round a 10 ms attack to nothing".

**What the code does:**

| Path | Fade in/out | Duck attack/release | Compressor attack/release |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set_audio` over MCP (the agent) | stored exactly | stored exactly | stored exactly |
| Audio inspector rows | **snapped to a frame** | **snapped to a frame** | stored exactly |
| Dragging a fade handle on the timeline | snapped to a frame | — | — |

**The effect.** Typing a 0.01 s Duck Attack in the inspector at 30 fps stores 0. The nearest frame is 0 ms, because a frame is 33 ms long. Sending the same value through `set_audio` stores 0.01 s (6000 ticks). At 24 fps, a 0.1 s attack typed in the inspector becomes 0.083 s.

This also breaks the rule that the UI and the agent produce the same result for the same edit. The compressor rows in the same pane already skip the snap, and their comment says they differ from "every other time in this pane".

**Why I didn't fix it in the dedup work.** The audit only found that the inspector's seconds-to-frame helper is copied in about five places, which would save roughly 8 lines. The real finding is that two audio sections should probably stop snapping at all. That changes behaviour, so the project rules require recording the decision in spec §11 before writing the code.

**The decision needed:**
1. **Stop snapping duck attack and release (recommended).** They are dynamics times like the compressor's, and no frame lines them up visually. A 10–50 ms attack is a normal value, and today it can't be typed.
2. **Fades in the inspector.** I'd also stop snapping these to match the core and the agent, which can already set off-grid fades.
3. **Fade handle drag on the timeline.** I'd keep the snap. A drag snapping to frames is a normal gesture convention, and the handle's position is drawn against the frame grid. If you choose this, I'll write it into the §11 entry as a deliberate exception.

If you agree with all three, I'll add the §11 entry and make the change as the last item in the queue. Changes 1 and 2 drop the snap call in `fadeSection` and `duckSection`. The small shared `frameTicks(seconds:)` helper for the remaining inspector sections would go in alongside. Or tell me to keep the current behaviour, and I'll record that decision in §11 instead and close #355.

Since 2026-10-10 the backlog lanes run each batch as a headless `claude -p` process (`~/.claude/litecode/rasterize/driver/run_lane.py <lane> <handoff>`), and the controller conversation only plans batches, rules on STOPs and integrates with `driver/integrate.py`. The procedure is in the orchestrator state file ([[backlog-orchestrator-state-file]]).

**Why:** the controller conversation filled its context from subagent hand-backs; the user wants runs that last overnight while keeping a controller with cross-lane context (they rejected fully stateless per-run controllers and single-issue runs: batch small/related issues together).

**How to apply:** launch lane runs in the background, read only their few printed lines, integrate one at a time and check the exit code before anything else, then plan the next batch with the other lanes' in-flight work in view. See [[parallel-worktree-lanes]] and [[lane-split-big-and-small]].

**Lanes run to closure (user, 2026-10-10: "Why is the lane ending if the issue isn't closed?").** A take outside its build table is not a STOP: the lane refits and retakes (up to 3 per item) and builds; batch-sized remainders are built in the same run; near-match rule self-applied. STOP only for a denied action, a stalled Photoshop, a genuine user decision, or a third take without a verdict; commit what's done first. Don't write requests that split an issue into phases or allow "comment only" endings.

**Usage limits (2026-10-10):** run_lane.py now treats a 429 / "usage_limit_reached" / "session limit" result as a wait until the reset time named in the message (+2 min), not as a failed attempt; before the fix three lanes burned all retries in 40 minutes. The user may switch accounts to reset the limit; a live `claude -p` older than a few seconds is working, not limited.

**The user pushes main to origin themselves (confirmed 2026-10-11), at any time.** A lane commit whose message says `Closes #N` closes that issue on GitHub when it is pushed, even if I merged it as comment-only (#458 closed early that way and had to be reopened). **How to apply:** on a comment-only merge, strip `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` from the lane's commit message before integrating.

**Launch rule (owner, binding):** a lane is launched ONLY as its own Bash tool call with `run_in_background` and `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` — never `&` inside a Bash command, and never a `run_lane.py` line appended to another command. I broke this twice in Oct 2026 (killed my own pids at once).

`make gate` ends with the `probes` step: the same type check of each probe set whose directory under `scripts/` has uncommitted changes, and of each set whose last type check failed, until it passes. The step fails on a `scripts/` directory that holds Swift and is in neither `PROBE_SETS` nor `STANDALONE_DIRS` of `scripts/probe_build.py`.

`make gate` takes `GATE_ARGS="--force"` to run every step; the probes step still covers only probe directories that changed or failed last time, so a committed probe directory is checked with `python3 scripts/probe_build.py --typecheck scripts/<probe dir>`. It returns non-zero for any outcome but a pass, and its last line says which: `gate: FAIL (<steps>)` names the failing steps (`(gate)` means the script itself raised, with the traceback on stderr); `gate: BLOCKED ...` means another build, test run or gate in this checkout was running and nothing ran, so run it again when that one ends. Logs are `build/gate-logs/<step>.log`.

### Parallel worktrees

- Batches run in parallel lanes: the main checkout and git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/lane-*`. Each lane builds its own `core/target` and `build/`.
- `make gate` holds its own checkout's `build/gate.lock` and waits only for builds, test runs and gates in that checkout, never another lane's.
- The Photoshop probe lock (`run_photoshop.probe_lock()`, a machine-wide `flock`; see `scripts/photoshop-probe/README.md`) serializes Photoshop takes across lanes.
- Wall-clock measurements (`make cancel-bench`, the time-measuring Release-only drives) need the machine idle: run them only when no other lane is building.
- Lanes need no MCP port ranges (#430): the agent server listens only on a Unix socket, and every owned instance gets a private scratch socket of its own (`mcp_client.scratch_socket()`), so two lanes' instances never meet.

## Driving a built app for verification

The MCP server is the reliable way to exercise the app end-to-end (open documents, run tools, render the canvas as PNG, check undo). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run one lane batch as a headless `claude -p` run, retrying transient failures.

    run_lane.py <lane a|b|c|d> <handoff dir>

The controller conversation writes <handoff>/request.md (and, after a STOP,
a RULING-*.md), then launches this in the background. The run drives the
litecode pipeline in the lane's worktree and ends by writing <handoff>/RESULT.md
(`status: ready | stopped | failed`). This script prints at most a few lines,
so the controller's context grows by a line per batch, not by the pipeline.

Transient failures (API/network errors, usage limits, a run that ended
without RESULT.md) are retried with backoff; each retry resumes the pipeline
from the handoff files. Every run's JSON is kept in <handoff>/runs/.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path('/Users/kevingalligan/devel/rasterize')
DRIVER = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PORTS = {'a': '47xx', 'b': '48xx', 'c': '49xx', 'd': '50xx'}
RUN_TIMEOUT = 8 * 3600
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 6
# Variables that tie a child to this controller session; a lane run is its own session.
STRIP = ('CLAUDECODE', 'CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID', 'CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION',
         'CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED', 'CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET',
         'CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN', 'CLAUDE_PID', 'CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT')
DENY = [
    'Bash(git push*)', 'Bash(git stash)', 'Bash(git stash pop*)', 'Bash(git rebase main*)',
    'Bash(git merge *)', 'Bash(gh issue close*)', 'Bash(gh issue comment*)',
    'Bash(gh issue edit*)', 'Bash(gh pr*)', 'Bash(kill *)', 'Bash(pkill *)',
    'Bash(killall *)', 'Bash(*gimp*)', 'Bash(*GIMP*)', 'Bash(*_ui.py*)',
]



MAX_LIMIT_WAITS = 24


def until_reset(blob: str) -> int:
    """Seconds until a 'resets 6:50pm' time named in a limit message, plus two
    minutes; 30 minutes when no time is named. Capped at six hours."""
    import datetime
    import re
    m = re.search(r'resets\s+(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*([ap]m)', blob)
    if not m:
        return 1800
    hour, minute = int(m.group(1)) % 12, int(m.group(2) or 0)
    if m.group(3) == 'pm':
        hour += 12
    now = datetime.datetime.now()
    reset = now.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0)
    if reset <= now:
        reset += datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    return min(int((reset - now).total_seconds()) + 120, 6 * 3600)

def result_status(handoff: Path):
    path = handoff / 'RESULT.md'
    if not path.exists():
        return None, ''
    text = path.read_text()
    first = text.strip().splitlines()[0] if text.strip() else ''
    status = first.split(':', 1)[1].strip() if first.startswith('status:') else 'unknown'
    return status, text


def main():
    lane, handoff = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2]).expanduser().resolve()
    worktree = REPO / '.claude' / 'worktrees' / f'lane-{lane}'
    assert worktree.is_dir(), f'no worktree {worktree}'
    assert (handoff / 'request.md').exists(), f'no request.md in {handoff}'
    # A lane with no work of its own starts its batch on the current main.
    dirty = subprocess.run(['git', 'status', '--porcelain'], cwd=worktree,
                           capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    behind = subprocess.run(['git', 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', 'HEAD', 'main'],
                            cwd=worktree).returncode == 0
    if not dirty and behind:
        subprocess.run(['git', 'merge', '--ff-only', '-q', 'main'], cwd=worktree, check=True)
    stale = handoff / 'RESULT.md'
    if stale.exists():
        stale.rename(handoff / f'RESULT-{int(stale.stat().st_mtime)}.md')
    (handoff / 'runs').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    prompt = (DRIVER / 'lane-prompt.md').read_text().format(
        lane=lane.upper(), worktree=worktree, branch=f'lane-{lane}', ports=PORTS[lane],
        handoff=handoff, rules=DRIVER / 'rules.md')
    settings = json.dumps({'permissions': {'deny': DENY}})
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in STRIP}
    env['RZ_BACKGROUND'] = '1'
    started, cost, waits = time.time(), 0.0, []
    attempt, limit_waits = 0, 0
    while attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS:
        attempt += 1
        stamp = time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')
        cmd = ['claude', '-p', prompt, '--output-format', 'json',
               '--permission-mode', 'auto', '--settings', settings]
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=worktree, env=env, capture_output=True,
                                  text=True, timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT)
            out, err, code = proc.stdout, proc.stderr, proc.returncode
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
            out, err, code = (e.stdout or b'').decode() if isinstance(e.stdout, bytes) else (e.stdout or ''), 'timeout', -1
        (handoff / 'runs' / f'{stamp}.json').write_text(out or '')
        if err:
            (handoff / 'runs' / f'{stamp}.stderr').write_text(err)
        try:
            data = json.loads(out)
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
            data = {}
        cost += float(data.get('total_cost_usd') or 0)
        status, _ = result_status(handoff)
        if status in ('ready', 'stopped', 'failed'):
            break
        blob = f"{data.get('result', '')} {data.get('api_error', '')} {err}".lower()
        limited = (data.get('api_error_status') == 429 or any(w in blob for w in (
            'usage limit', 'usage_limit', 'rate limit', 'limit reached', 'session limit',
            'hit your', 'overloaded')))
        if limited and limit_waits < MAX_LIMIT_WAITS:
            # A usage limit is not a failure of the run: wait for the reset and
            # do not spend one of the MAX_ATTEMPTS on it.
            limit_waits += 1
            attempt -= 1
            wait = until_reset(blob)
            waits.append(f'limit {limit_waits}: wait {wait}s ({time.strftime("%H:%M")})')
            time.sleep(wait)
            continue
        wait = min(120 * attempt, 900)
        waits.append(f'attempt {attempt}: code {code}, error/no RESULT, wait {wait}s')
        if attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS:
            time.sleep(wait)
    status, text = result_status(handoff)
    minutes = (time.time() - started) / 60
    summary = [l for l in text.strip().splitlines()[1:6]] if text else []
    print(f'lane-{lane} {status or "no-result"} after {minutes:.0f} min, ${cost:.2f}, '
          f'{attempt} attempt(s): {handoff}')
    for line in summary:
        print('  ' + line[:300])
    for w in waits:
        print('  retry ' + w)
    with open(DRIVER / 'runs.jsonl', 'a') as log:
        log.write(json.dumps({'lane': lane, 'handoff': str(handoff), 'status': status,
                              'minutes': round(minutes), 'cost': round(cost, 2),
                              'attempts': attempt, 'ended': time.strftime('%F %T')}) + '\n')
    sys.exit(0 if status == 'ready' else 1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Integrate a ready lane batch: rebase onto main, gate, drives, ff-merge, issue comments.

    integrate.py <lane a|b|c|d> <handoff dir> [--continue]

Run by the controller conversation after a lane run reports `status: ready`.
Nothing merges unless `make gate` ends `gate: PASS` and every drive in
<handoff>/integrate.json exits 0 with its expected text. Exit codes:
  0 merged and commented; 3 rebase conflict (resolve in the worktree, then
  rerun with --continue); 4 gate or a drive failed (nothing merged);
  5 precondition failed. Output is a few lines; logs go to <handoff>/integrate/.
"""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path('/Users/kevingalligan/devel/rasterize')
DRIVER = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def run(cmd, cwd, log=None, shell=False, check=False):
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, shell=shell, capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = proc.stdout + proc.stderr
    if log:
        log.write_text(out)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f'failed: {cmd}\n{out[-1500:]}')
    return proc.returncode, out


def git(args, cwd, check=True):
    """git with one retry on a transient index.lock."""
    code, out = run(['git'] + args, cwd)
    if code != 0 and 'index.lock' in out:
        time.sleep(3)
        code, out = run(['git'] + args, cwd)
    if check and code != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f'git {" ".join(args)} failed:\n{out[-1500:]}')
    return code, out


def done(code, lines):
    for line in lines:
        print(line)
    sys.exit(code)


def main():
    lane, handoff = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2]).expanduser().resolve()
    cont = '--continue' in sys.argv[3:]
    worktree = REPO / '.claude' / 'worktrees' / f'lane-{lane}'
    branch = f'lane-{lane}'
    logs = handoff / 'integrate'
    logs.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    plan = json.loads((handoff / 'integrate.json').read_text())

    # Untracked files (the user's own downloads, say) cannot be lost by the
    # fast-forward: git refuses a merge that would overwrite one.
    if run(['git', 'status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=no'], REPO)[1].strip():
        done(5, ['main checkout is dirty; nothing done'])
    if cont:
        for marker in ('rebase-merge', 'rebase-apply'):
            path = run(['git', 'rev-parse', '--git-path', marker], worktree)[1].strip()
            if (worktree / path).exists() or Path(path).exists():
                done(3, ['rebase still in progress in ' + str(worktree)])
    else:
        if run(['git', 'status', '--porcelain'], worktree)[1].strip():
            done(5, [f'{branch} worktree has uncommitted changes; commit them first'])
        if git(['rev-list', '--count', f'main..{branch}'], REPO)[1].strip() == '0':
            done(5, [f'{branch} has no commits ahead of main'])
        code, out = git(['rebase', 'main'], worktree, check=False)
        if code != 0:
            conflicts = run(['git', 'diff', '--name-only', '--diff-filter=U'], worktree)[1].split()
            done(3, [f'{branch}: rebase conflict in {len(conflicts)} file(s): ' + ', '.join(conflicts),
                     f'resolve in {worktree}, `git rebase --continue`, then rerun with --continue'])

    while True:
        code, out = run(['make', 'gate'], worktree, log=logs / 'gate.log')
        last = out.strip().splitlines()[-1] if out.strip() else ''
        if 'BLOCKED' in last:
            time.sleep(60)
            continue
        break
    if code != 0 or not last.startswith('gate: PASS'):
        done(4, [f'{branch}: {last or "gate produced no output"}; nothing merged (log {logs / "gate.log"})'])

    for i, drive in enumerate(plan.get('drives', [])):
        log = logs / f'drive-{i}.log'
        code, out = run(drive['cmd'], worktree, log=log, shell=True)
        expect = drive.get('expect') or ''
        if code != 0 or (expect and expect not in out):
            tail = out.strip().splitlines()[-1] if out.strip() else ''
            done(4, [f'{branch}: drive failed: {drive["cmd"][:160]}', f'  exit {code}: {tail[:200]} (log {log})'])

    git(['merge', '--ff-only', branch], REPO)
    head = git(['rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'], REPO)[1].strip()
    tip = git(['rev-parse', '--short', branch], REPO)[1].strip()
    if head != tip:
        done(5, [f'main is {head} but {branch} is {tip}; check the merge'])

    posted = []
    # A "create" entry files a new issue first; its number replaces
    # {{AFTER_V1}} in every other body (a closing comment that points to it).
    issues = plan.get('issues', [])
    created = ''
    for issue in [i for i in issues if i['action'] == 'create']:
        body_path = logs / 'issue-create.md'
        body_path.write_text((handoff / issue['body_file']).read_text().replace('{{HASH}}', head))
        cmd = ['gh', 'issue', 'create', '--title', issue['title'], '--body-file', str(body_path)]
        for label in issue.get('labels', []):
            cmd += ['--label', label]
        code, out = run(cmd, REPO)
        created = out.strip().rsplit('/', 1)[-1] if code == 0 else ''
        posted.append(f'created #{created}' if created else f'create FAILED: {out.strip()[-160:]}')
    for issue in [i for i in issues if i['action'] != 'create']:
        body = (handoff / issue['body_file']).read_text().replace('{{HASH}}', head)
        if created:
            body = body.replace('{{AFTER_V1}}', f'#{created}')
        body_path = logs / f'comment-{issue["number"]}.md'
        body_path.write_text(body)
        if issue['action'] == 'close':
            code, out = run(['gh', 'issue', 'close', str(issue['number']), '--comment', body], REPO)
        else:
            code, out = run(['gh', 'issue', 'comment', str(issue['number']), '--body-file', str(body_path)], REPO)
        posted.append(f'#{issue["number"]} {issue["action"]}{"" if code == 0 else " FAILED: " + out.strip()[-160:]}')
    subject = git(['log', '-1', '--format=%s', head], REPO)[1].strip()
    with open(DRIVER / 'merges.log', 'a') as log:
        log.write(f'{time.strftime("%F %T")} {head} lane-{lane} {subject}\n')
    done(0, [f'{branch} merged: main = {head} {subject[:150]}', '  ' + '; '.join(posted)])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

---
name: parallel-worktree-lanes
description: Owner 2026-10-25 — run independent issues in parallel worktree lanes like ~/devel/rasterize, one orchestrator integrating onto main one at a time
metadata:

---

The owner asked on 2026-10-25, during the dedup queue: "Run changes in multiple worktree lanes, similar to how ~/devel/rasterize works on multiple tasks". Rasterize runs three lanes (a, b, c), each a worktree on its own branch. Each lane runs one batch at a time through litecode, and a single controller rebases each finished batch onto main, re-gates it and fast-forwards main. Nothing is pushed.

**Why:** throughput. Running issues one at a time leaves the machine (12 cores, 96 GB) idle.

**How to apply:**
- Put lane worktrees outside the repo: `~/devel/framejob-lane-<x>`. CoW-copy `tools/proof/media`, `agent/node_modules` and `tools/proof/work` into each with `cp -cR`. Run `make rust` in each before the first gate, so a cold build doesn't hit the 600 s cap.
- Split lanes by area so their files don't overlap.
- Run the lanes as one Workflow: issues within a lane run in sequence, and integration is serialized behind a JS mutex.
- Keep three lanes at most. Disk is tight: about 55 GB free, and each lane needs about 6 GB of build products.
- Main stays clean and is only ever fast-forwarded.

Related: [[feature-worktree-merge-per-phase]], [[litecode-stacked-phases]], [[dedup-audit-2026-10-25]].
EOF

The work now runs in three lanes, each a separate worktree on its own branch, as in rasterize:

| Lane | Worktree | Issues, in order | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `~/devel/framejob-dedup` | #358 (being implemented) → #355 | me, in this session |
| B | `~/devel/framejob-lane-b` | #360 → #361 → #364 | a background workflow |
| C | `~/devel/framejob-lane-c` | #359 → #362 → #363 | the same workflow |

**How lanes B and C run:**
- Each issue goes through implement and review, with up to 5 fix passes.
- An integrating agent then adds the CLAUDE.md edits the issue needs, commits on the lane's branch and rebases onto main. It runs `make gate` in that lane, fast-forwards main and closes the issue.
- Only one lane merges at a time. If a lane hits a stop or a failed gate, that lane halts; the other keeps going.

**Merge safety:** my lane A merges are also fast-forward only. If main has moved, I rebase and run the gate again.

**Setup:** both new lanes have their proof media and the assistant helper's packages, copied without using extra disk, and their Rust core is already built. Lanes B and C were split so they don't edit the same source files. They do append to some shared docs, such as `tools/proof/README.md`, and the integrating agent resolves those clashes by keeping both sides.

**Disk:** about 55 GB is free. Each lane adds about 6 GB of build output as it goes, which is why I stopped at three lanes. Nothing gets pushed.

The lane layout is in `~/.claude/litecode/framejob/dedup-STATE.md`, and I saved this way of working to memory for future runs.

The open list is short: 31 issues, 15 of them icebox. Here's what I'd do next, in order.

**1. Audio accuracy for retimed clips.** These are real defects in features that already shipped:
- **#337:** a retimed clip's exported audio comes out a different length from the timeline, and the error varies between runs. At ×2 it is up to +85 ms; at ×0.5 with keep pitch it is up to −25 ms.
- **#334:** a constant ×4 clip's exported audio has sample steps.
- **#335:** during playback, the audio of a ×1 clip is read 21 ms early, while its export is not.

I'd leave **#299** (keep pitch moving sound off the timeline) alone: you already chose to keep Apple's time-pitch as it is.

**2. Speed-ramp follow-ups,** both features:
- **#341:** re-time existing captions after a speed or ramp edit. Today they drift off the words.
- **#339:** draw a speed ramp's rate graph on the action lane.

**3. Proof leftovers,** small:
- **#329:** two of the graphics-performance guards from #127 have no proof that fails without them.
- **#330:** the HDR proof's gain-map peak test only catches its fault through the bands' order.

These would run well as three lanes at once, the way this round did: A takes #337, #334 and #335 (the audio engine); B takes #341 (captions); C takes #339 and then #329 and #330. The areas barely overlap.

**Waiting on you, no code needed:**
- **#131** (opening a project whose media moved fails instead of offering Relink) needs a repro or a project from you.
- **#318–#320** need camera originals in Sony S-Log3, Panasonic V-Log and Canon Log 2/3, for the camera log curves in #278. You shoot a GH5, so a V-Log clip would unblock #319 if the GH5 has V-Log installed.

**Left alone:**
- **#328,** graphics speed: parked, since your rule is features before performance.
- Everything in icebox.

# Spec: #341, re-time existing captions after a speed or ramp edit (STOPPED for the owner)

## Goal
Captions already on the timeline follow a speed or ramp edit of the clip they caption, in the same undo step and with the MCP mirror. Alternatively the owner rules that regenerating stays the way.

## What the tree says (lane-b HEAD 3f7c948; re-measured, not taken from the issue)
- **A caption has no link to the clip it came from.** A caption is an ordinary text clip (`add_text_clip` in `CaptionLayout.place`, `app/Sources/CaptionLayout.swift:243`). `Clip` (`core/src/model.rs:262`) and `TextProps` (`core/src/model_text.rs:73`) have no origin field. `TextProps.words` are clip-time offsets inside the caption clip (spec §11 W-3). Captions do not follow ANY edit of their clip today, `move_clip` and trims included, so #341 would be the first edit they follow.
- **The one "which captions belong to a run" rule is inferred.** `CaptionLayout.replaceableTracks` (`CaptionLayout.swift:375`), Generate Captions' "Replace existing" restyle, uses it: the track is named "Captions" or "Captions N", holds only text clips, and every clip on it overlaps a job's span. An imported `.srt` lands on a track named the same way, and so does a hand-made text clip on such a track.
- **Transcripts and fillers already follow.** `get_transcript`, `transcribe`, `detect_fillers` and `detect_silence` read the clip's CURRENT map at call time (`Transcriber.jobs(…, maps:)` in `app/Sources/Transcriber+Jobs.swift:97`, `AgentServer+Transcript.swift:52`, `MediaPeaks.sourceTick`). A filler cut is a `ripple_delete_ranges` already applied, so nothing is left to re-time. The issue's list therefore reduces to caption clips: subtitle cues and word-caption pages.
- **Edits that change a clip's map** (all keep the clip's `start`): `set_speed` and `rate_stretch` change `duration` too, and never ripple (`core/src/edit_clip_timing.rs:229,283`). `set_action_end {speed}` and `add_speed_ramp` (SR-23) keep the slot (SR-2), so a ramp edit moves the clip's OUT point in source. `set_action` and `remove_action` on a speed action do the same, and so do the action lane's band drags.
- **Seams that already exist.** Every speed edit a person makes goes through `SpeedAudioDrop.commit` (`app/Sources/SpeedAudioDrop.swift`: the Speed sheet, the Speed Ramp sheet, the inspector) or `EditorViewController+SpeedAudio.swift` (the ⌥-drag rate stretch's live edit). Both already compare a pure trial against the base. An agent's op tool answer gains fields at `AgentServer.swift:686` (frozen file, wiring only) and `AgentServer+Actions.swift:135` (`SpeedAudioDrop.answerFields`). `rc_project_source_map` answers both maps (old handle, new handle), and `SourceMap` (`app/Sources/SourceMap.swift`) reads them both ways, so no rate is computed in Swift (D2-1).
- **Re-timing cannot always be complete.** Some edits play MORE source in the same slot: a faster end rate in a ramp, or a speed-up whose slot is held. Those words were never transcribed, so no caption exists to move, and only regenerating captions them. Other edits play LESS source, so captions for words past the new out point have nowhere to go. A slow-down by `set_speed` lengthens the clip, and its re-timed captions can then run into captions of the next clip on the same caption track.

## Options
- **A. Regenerating stays the way.** Close #341 as decided (rule O / SR-20 (g) stand unchanged). This needs a §11 line recording the owner's choice and a sentence in the captions guide page: "after a speed change, Generate Captions… with Replace existing". No code.
- **B. Perform automatically (recommended).** Each edit in the map-changing list above re-times, in the same undo step, every caption clip on a caption-named track (the `replaceableTracks` name and only-text rule) that lies wholly inside the edited clip's span before the edit. Each caption's start, end and word times are mapped old clip time → source (old map) → new clip time (new map), then snapped to the frame grid as `CaptionLayout.place` snaps. Ops are `move_clip`/`trim_*` and a `set_text` of `words`. A person's edit adds nothing to the UI. An agent's op tool answer gains `captions_retimed: [ids]` and `captions_removed: [ids]`. Sub-rules, decided as part of B:
  1. A caption whose source the clip no longer plays is removed, and its words after the new out point are cut from a word page, in the same step. The answer, and for a person the undo name ("Set Speed and Re-time Captions"), says so.
  2. Source newly revealed is left uncaptioned. The guide says to regenerate for it.
  3. A re-timed caption that would overlap a caption it was not moved with is cut back to abut it (`place`'s rule 4). If that leaves it under a frame, it is removed and reported.
  Why recommended: it meets the done-when with no question and no format bump. It is the same for a person and an agent ("a tool call never asking", roadmap-14), undo takes it back with the edit, and it finds captions by the rule the restyle already uses. Risk: a hand-made text clip on a "Captions" track over the clip moves with it.
- **C. Offer.** After a person's speed edit over captioned speech, an alert asks "Re-time N captions?" (`SpeedAudioDrop.ask`'s shape, a second question beside the ×12 one). An agent passes a new `retime_captions: true` on the six op tools, declared in `AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift`, because a tool call cannot be asked. Finding captions, the maths and B's sub-rules are the same. It costs a second alert on every speed edit over captions, and a tool argument that its op does not take.
- **D. A stored link.** Add `text.caption_of: <clip id>` (format 28, schema_v28) to every caption Generate Captions makes. Re-time exactly the linked clips (as B or C), and let a later road map have captions follow move, trim, split and ripple too. This is the most exact of the four. It needs a persisted field, a migration (older captions have no link, so they fall back to B's rule or nothing), and paste, duplicate and nest carries. It is a road map, not a batch.

## What B (or C) would touch, for the next spec once the owner answers
- `app/Sources/CaptionRetime.swift` (new, ≤ 400): finding the captions, mapping through both `SourceMap`s, and the ops.
- `app/Sources/SpeedAudioDrop.swift` and `app/Sources/EditorViewController+SpeedAudio.swift`: the person's doors append the re-time ops to the same grouped edit.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+Actions.swift`, plus one wiring line in `app/Sources/AgentServer.swift`: the agent's answer fields and the appended ops.
- Catalog prose for `set_speed`, `rate_stretch`, `set_action_end`, `set_action`, `remove_action` and `add_speed_ramp`, and under C one row per tool in `AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift`.
- A probe `tools/proof/caption_retime_probe.swift` (via `swift_build.py`) and MCP rows over `get_project`.
- Spec §11: a new SR-26 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/speed-ramps-3.md`, with Amended-by lines on SR-20 (g) and rule O. Also spec §6/§7.9 prose for the answer fields, `docs/guide/` (captions and speed pages), and a `docs/manual-checks.md` row if a person must judge how the re-timed captions read.
- No core change, FFI change or format bump under B or C.

## Verification (for the follow-up spec)
Targeted: `python3 tools/proof/swift_build.py typecheck tools/proof/caption_retime_probe.swift`, then `make typecheck` (seconds; baseline 0 errors, 4 warnings).
Full: `make gate` (once, in the foreground, under the 600 s cap; `make app` ~90 s inside it). Then the change's MCP proof against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`). It covers: caption clips' starts, durations and word times read back through `get_project` after each map-changing op, and the same step undone.

## Out of scope
- Captions following move, trim, split or ripple (option D's later road map).
- Re-transcribing source a ramp newly reveals (B sub-rule 2).
- Any change to how transcripts, fillers or silences are placed. They already read the current map.
Investigated in 1dc75b2 (main, not pushed); not fixed, owner question below. retimed_audio_proof.py B2 (2026-10-25, Debug and Release) read the plan's mix through AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput with no writer, for C-off-x4 (×4, Keep pitch off, 4 s of a 220 Hz sine):
- the 16-bit read the writer uses had 28 / 24 step events, the float read 27 / 28, and the same read with the output's audioTimePitchAlgorithm = .varispeed 31 / 27;
- the events are about 0.17 s apart (≈ 8 192 output frames), within ≈ 1 ms of a reader chunk boundary, and move from read to read (an export and an app read of the same project differ from frame 279 / 5 399 / 10 521);
- against RampAudioRenderer's ×4 ideal, max |diff| ≈ 0.50; the clicks fixture's placement passes (79–80/80, +0.016 ms).

So the steps are inside AVFoundation's own read and Frame Job's writer cannot remove them. B1 stays reported, not scored, until this is answered.

**Owner question:** (a) render every constant Keep pitch off time-scaled segment offline like a ramp (SR-6's renderer, silent until rendered, an export waiting for it, the cache and its ledger), or (b) accept the limit and record it in spec §11. No recommendation until (a)'s cost is measured: render wall time and cache size per minute of ×N audio, and the silent-until-rendered window in preview.

What is left: the owner's choice, then either (a)'s build or (b)'s §11 entry.
